newsitem.title: UK: UK's Labour unveils new deal for nurses.
newsitem.headline: UK's Labour unveils new deal for nurses.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party on Friday unveiled a new plan for nurses in the health service but the government quickly said there was no new money involved.

Shadow Health Secretary Chris Smith fired the latest shot in the phoney war of the pre-election campaign, telling reporters that Labour's policies will stop the drain of nurses from the National Health Service. "Labour will provide nurses with a safer, more flexible working environment," he said.

Labour's new deal will offer better job security with flexible work options, the support of legal action against people who assault nurses, a national system for pay and wider opportunities for professional development.

Smith also said a Labour government would ban gagging clauses from NHS contracts, allowing nurses to play a fuller role in key health service decisions. "By listening to the needs of nurses, by offering them the support and encouragement they deserve, and by allowing them to carry out the job for which they are trained, we will restore their morale and ensure that patients have the best care available," he said.

But where is the money coming from, asked government health minister Gerry Malone. "Mr Smith is today delivering an insult to nurses. He is claiming that he can raise morale without committing a penny extra," he said.

A Labour Party source said that missed the point. Labour had listened to the grievances of nurses and will act to improve their working environment. That would not necessarily need huge amounts of cash.
Shadow Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown has pledged to stick to the Conservative government's spending plans for the next two years.
"The Tories are destroying the NHS," Smith said. "We will cut waiting lists by cutting bureaucracy and restore the morale of those who work in the NHS."
Elections must be held by May 22 but Prime Minister John Major is believed to favour May 1.
